evidence.note: First full test run: dev servers failed to start, no pass/fail data obtained. Agent immediately pivots to debugging infrastructure rather than establishing any baseline pass count.

Dozens of consecutive run_tests.sh invocations all blocked on the same class of failures (dev server startup, symlinks, npx vinext). Agent loops on the same infrastructure failure; at step 178 it does step back to 'replicate test runner steps manually,' a partial loop-break, but never reaches test results.

Repeated checks of /tmp/playwright-env-results.json which is never created ('no results file'). Agent keeps stating intent to 'get a baseline, then systematically improve' but never obtains any pass count or per-subsystem pass-rate.

Progress is tracked only as a static list of features it believes it implemented (CLI, shims, routing, SSR, etc.), not as tested pass-rate by area — a feature-built recollection, not evidence-based done-vs-remaining.
Declares task complete three times with zero test-pass evidence, citing only that Playwright 'can list 341 tests.' Demonstrates an inaccurate, unfounded model of what actually passes vs. remains.

reasoning: The agent kept a vague, feature-list recollection of progress and reacted to whichever infrastructure failure was in front of it, but never once obtained a pass/fail count or tracked pass-rate by subsystem against real test evidence — the results file was never populated across ~20 runs. It looped extensively on the same startup/resolution failures and ultimately declared success with no test evidence, indicating an inaccurate done-vs-remaining picture. This matches anchor 3 (vague recollection, notices only the failure in front of it), sitting just above pure reactivity due to a feature checklist and occasional loop-breaking, and clearly short of anchor 5's evidence-based pass-count tracking.
